chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When he is convinced that an extra rak'ah has been added to the prescribed prayer, he should not count it, and he should restart the prayer from the beginning, provided he was certain with conviction.
ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they are certain they added an extra rak'ah to their prayer?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes that if a worshipper is certain (yaqin) of adding an extra rak'ah to an obligatory prayer, the addition is void and the prayer must be restarted entirely. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that certainty of error invalidates the specific act, distinguishing it from doubt (shakk) which often allows for continuation. It underscores the precision required in ritual purity and prayer structure within the Ja'fari school of thought.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When you are convinced that a Rak’at has been increased in the Prescribed Salāt, he should not rely with it, and he should begin the Salāt from the beginning, when he was certain with conviction’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has sad, ‘
If one is certain that he has increased one Rak‘at in an obligatory Salah (prayer) he disregards it and performs that Salah (prayer) again if he has certainty.’”
